Paradise Fire & the Mill Creek Watershed

A Paradise Fire snapshot integrating official fire perimeters, thermal detections, weather, Sentinel-2 imagery, and preliminary burn-severity mapping.

Unofficial report: This analytical report is not an emergency notification and should not be used as the sole basis for evacuation, public-safety, firefighting, incident-command, engineering, treatment, hydrologic, erosion or debris-flow decisions.

For the most current official fire information, visit InciWeb. For evacuation notices, use Umatilla County Emergency Advisories. Additional incident updates are available from the Paradise Fire Facebook page and Watch Duty.

Paradise Fire preliminary burn-severity mapping

The burn-severity maps included in this report are preliminary, satellite-derived Burned Area Reflectance Classification products for the Paradise Fire. They are not official or field-validated Soil Burn Severity products. They are intended for preliminary visualization and to provide an initial indication of possible fire effects within the Mill Creek municipal watershed.

The maps follow the general workflow described by the joint USGS–USDA Forest Service BAER Imagery Support Program. An initial BARC is generated from satellite imagery and subsequently reviewed and adjusted by BAER personnel using field observations. A final Soil Burn Severity map is created only after that assessment.

The preliminary classification uses the starting values demonstrated in the official BAER training document Exercise 2: Editing the BARC:

Preliminary classBARC256 rangeApproximate dNBR range2024+ BAER color
Unburned/very low0–77≤0.110Dark blue-green
Low78–1220.115–0.335Light blue-green
Moderate123–1910.340–0.680Yellow
High192–255≥0.685Dark red

These values are starting points from an official training example, not mandatory national thresholds. BAER guidance describes the initial BARC4 as an analyst’s first approximation. BAER teams frequently modify the class breakpoints and mapped areas using field sampling, reconnaissance and professional judgment.

The maps use the color-vision-deficiency-friendly, Section 508 palette identified by the BAER FAQ for 2024 and later.

Preliminary Burn Severity area

Classification is applied to BARC256 integer ranges derived from dNBR using the BAER training example above.

Selected Sentinel-2 scenes

Important limitations

These preliminary maps are not definitive measurements of soil and vegetation burn severity and should not be used alone for hydrologic modeling, erosion or debris-flow estimates, treatment design, engineering or public-safety decisions.

Results may be affected by:

  • Active fire, hot surfaces, smoke, clouds and shadows
  • Changes in vegetation, soil and ash moisture
  • Rapid cooling, drying and ash redistribution
  • Image timing, resolution and alignment
  • Evolving fire perimeters and unvalidated thresholds
  • The absence of Paradise-specific field observations

Differences among map dates

Severity classes may differ between maps because each uses imagery acquired under different fire, atmospheric and surface conditions.

Expected Forest Service assessment

After fire activity decreases and safe field access becomes possible, Forest Service BAER specialists are expected to compare the preliminary BARC with observed soil and vegetation conditions, adjust thresholds and correct unreliable areas. The resulting field-reviewed Soil Burn Severity map will supersede these preliminary classifications.
